title: Summarize Cloud Concepts and Connectivity Options

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Cloud networking applies familiar network functions through virtual resources and provider services. Recognize the virtual network, its security controls and gateways, connection method, deployment and service models, and scaling behavior.
bullets: Network security groups and security lists
Public, private, and hybrid deployment models
SaaS, IaaS, and PaaS service models
sections.callout: Build the cloud network → protect it → connect it → choose the model → scale it.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Can you identify the virtual network component, security control, gateway, connectivity option, cloud model, or scaling characteristic described by a scenario?
bullets: Cloud traffic rules → Security group or security list
Provider/shared → Public; organization-controlled → Private; combination → Hybrid
Use → SaaS; infrastructure → IaaS; build/deploy → PaaS
Capacity growth → Scalability; dynamic demand response → Elasticity
Shared infrastructure with logical separation → Multitenancy

entries.title: Network Functions Virtualization (NFV)
paragraphs: NFV implements functions such as routers, firewalls, and load balancers in software rather than requiring a dedicated physical appliance for each function.
entries.memoryHook: Network function without a dedicated box.
entries.recognitionCue: A firewall runs as a virtualized network service → NFV.

entries.title: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
paragraphs: A VPC is a logically isolated virtual network within a cloud environment. It can contain address ranges, subnets, routes, security controls, and gateways.
entries.memoryHook: Your network space inside the cloud.
entries.recognitionCue: An organization needs an isolated network in a public cloud → VPC.

sections.title: Network Security Groups and Security Lists

entries.title: Network Security Group
paragraphs: A network security group applies permitted-traffic rules to associated cloud resources or interfaces. Exact behavior varies by provider, but the exam clue is a cloud-native traffic filter attached to resources.
entries.recognitionCue: Apply inbound and outbound rules to a workload → Network security group.

entries.title: Network Security List
paragraphs: A network security list applies traffic rules at a cloud network or subnet boundary, depending on the provider's design.
entries.recognitionCue: Apply rules to traffic entering or leaving a subnet → Network security list.

sections.callout: Both control cloud traffic; distinguish the resource-oriented or subnet-oriented scope described by the provider and scenario.

entries.title: Internet Gateway
paragraphs: An Internet gateway provides a path between a VPC and the Internet when routes and resource addressing permit it.
entries.recognitionCue: A public cloud resource needs direct Internet connectivity → Internet gateway.

entries.title: Network Address Translation (NAT) Gateway
paragraphs: A NAT gateway translates addresses so private resources can initiate outbound Internet connections without accepting unsolicited inbound connections directly.
entries.recognitionCue: A private instance must download updates without becoming publicly reachable → NAT gateway.

entries.title: Virtual Private Network (VPN)
paragraphs: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel between users or sites and a cloud environment, commonly across the public Internet.
entries.recognitionCue: Secure cloud connectivity over the Internet → VPN.

entries.title: Direct Connect
paragraphs: Direct Connect represents a dedicated private connection to cloud infrastructure instead of an Internet-based tunnel. Provider terminology and implementation can vary.
entries.recognitionCue: A predictable dedicated connection to the cloud is required → Direct Connect.

entries.title: Public Cloud
paragraphs: A provider operates shared infrastructure for multiple customers while tenant resources remain logically separated.
entries.recognitionCue: The organization consumes resources from a public provider → Public cloud.

entries.title: Private Cloud
paragraphs: Cloud infrastructure is dedicated to or controlled for one organization, whether hosted internally or by another party.
entries.recognitionCue: An organization requires dedicated cloud control → Private cloud.

entries.title: Hybrid Cloud
paragraphs: A hybrid model connects or combines public and private cloud environments so workloads or data can use both.
entries.recognitionCue: Private resources extend into provider cloud capacity → Hybrid cloud.

entries.title: Software as a Service (SaaS)
paragraphs: SaaS provides a finished application. The provider manages the underlying platform and infrastructure.
entries.recognitionCue: Users open a provider-hosted productivity application → SaaS.

entries.title: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
paragraphs: IaaS provides virtual machines, storage, and networking. The customer controls operating systems and workloads while the provider manages the physical infrastructure.
entries.recognitionCue: The customer configures virtual servers and networks → IaaS.

entries.title: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
paragraphs: PaaS provides a managed application-development and deployment platform so teams can build applications without managing all underlying infrastructure.
entries.memoryHook: Build and deploy on the platform.
entries.recognitionCue: Developers deploy code to a managed runtime → PaaS.

entries.title: Scalability
paragraphs: Scalability is the ability to increase or decrease processing, storage, or server capacity to support workload requirements.
entries.recognitionCue: Capacity can be expanded to support more users → Scalability.

entries.title: Elasticity
paragraphs: Elasticity is the dynamic expansion and contraction of resources in response to changing demand.
entries.recognitionCue: Resources automatically grow during a spike and shrink afterward → Elasticity.

entries.title: Multitenancy
paragraphs: Multitenancy allows multiple customers to share underlying cloud infrastructure while their environments remain logically separated.
entries.recognitionCue: Multiple organizations use one provider platform with logical isolation → Multitenancy.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Cloud resource traffic filter → Network security group
Subnet traffic filter → Network security list

entries.title: Internet Gateway vs. NAT Gateway
paragraphs: An Internet gateway provides Internet connectivity. A NAT gateway lets private resources initiate outbound traffic through address translation.

entries.title: VPN vs. Direct Connect
paragraphs: A VPN is an encrypted logical tunnel; Direct Connect is a dedicated connection.

entries.title: SaaS vs. PaaS vs. IaaS
paragraphs: Use software with SaaS, build and deploy with PaaS, and manage workloads on rented infrastructure with IaaS.

entries.title: Scalability vs. Elasticity
paragraphs: Scalability means capacity can change. Elasticity emphasizes dynamic adjustment as demand changes.
